Commentary.Commentary: That wraps up the formalities of the 5-match ODI series. Pakistan's lengthy tour of England will end with the one-off T20I between the two sides on 7th September at Old Trafford. The action starts at 2300 IST. Do tune in for our coverage of that contest. Until then, it's goodbye from us.

EOIN MORGAN doesn't regret the changes made today. Feels that Dawson's inclusion was made more with an eye towards the sub-continent tours later this year. Feels that his team has done really well throughout the series and even fought well in the defeat today. Ends by saying that he is happy with the team's passion.
The England players are receiving their medallions.

AZHAR ALI is relieved at Pakistan having won a game finally. Says that it's been a tough ODI series so far. Credits the bowlers for doing well especially in the death overs. Feels that his bowlers didn't bowl well in the start in helpful conditions but opines that Imad Wasim did really well to pull things back. He is very optimistic about Pakistan's future and says that there are many emerging talents in the side. However, he feels that backing the young guys is key.

JOE ROOT (MAN OF THE SERIES) feels that it's important to be consistent and contribute to the team's cause. Feels that it's been a great series for his side. Opines that England can still improve and become more powerful. States that playing fearlessly is key to his team's success and wants his mates to be more consistent in putting forward aggressive performances.

SARFRAZ AHMED (MAN OF THE MATCH) thanks God for his success and expresses pleasure at having contributed to his team's win. Feels that the nothing-to-lose situation allowed his side to play positive cricket. Lauds his senior partner Shoaib Malik for playing well. Reveals that the plan to attack debutant Dawson was purely intentional.

England did well to set a 300-plus target earlier in the day. They got off to a blazing start and kept it up for most of the game, thanks to a masterclass by Ben Stokes. However, Mohammad Amir and Hasan Ali slowed them down and Pakistan's brilliant death bowling kept them from adding even more to the score board.

While English captain Eoin Morgan made all the right calls, the bowlers were not able to restrict the flow of runs or break up vital partnerships. Mark Wood was the most impressive of the lot with ODI debutant Liam Dawson bringing in two crucial wickets but giving away too many runs.

Nearly all the credit for their fantastic revival lay in the hands of Sarfraz Ahmed and Shoaib Malik. The pair's 163-run partnership was the glue that held the innings together. They drove the fielding side to distraction as they tried their best to remove the partners. Their dismissals towards the end made for an interesting conclusion but their lower-middle order was enough to seal the deal.

A hard-fought innings and Pakistan have finally emerged the victors. Their lone win in the 5-match ODI series saves them from a whitewash and gives their supporters much to cheer about. Pakistan may have dodged a bullet but it was not completely smooth sailing. Babar Azam and Azhar Ali got Pakistan off to a quick start but their loss left the visitors shaken.

FOUR! POUNDED! Sharjeel is beginning to look more comfortable. Full around off, he stays in his place and drives it. It is a scooping shot and goes over mid off for a boundary.
Yorker on middle and off, defended to the bowler.
Fullish ball outside off, Sharjeel shifts his weight forward and drive it to mid off.
Fuller ball on off, Sharjeel looks to pull it but overestimates the bounce and bottom edges it onto his pads.
Back of a length ball on middle and off, pulled to square leg for a single.
Length ball around off, Azhar looks to work it but edges it onto his pads for a single.
Wide. Down the leg side and Azhar looks to play it but lets it through. The umpire spreads his arms and another single has been added to the total.
Fullish ball outside off, punched through the off side.
Short ball on off, defended from within the crease.
Length ball outside off, left alone.
FOUR! LUCKY RUNS! Down the leg side, Azhar works it off his pads. It goes to fine leg. The fielder dives to save it but misses and the ball crosses the ropes.
Better length this time, the ball passes inside the inside edge of the bat and Sharjeel is beaten.
FOUR! BEAUTIFUL SHOT! Length ball around off, Azhar waits for it and half-pulls it through mid-wicket. It was timed to perfection and goes all the way to the boundary.
Azhar has played it fine down the leg side for a  single.
Length ball around off, Azhar whips it over mid-wicket and has a lucky save as it goes just past the fielder. The batsmen get a couple.
Fuller ball outside off,  pushed to the cover region.
Back of a length ball outside off, defended off the back foot to the off side.
BEATEN! Again, Sharjeel goes back in the crease to defend it off the back foot but the ball beats his bat's outside edge.
BEATEN! Length ball outside off, the ball holds it's line to beat Sharjeel's bat's outside edge.
Length ball outside off, defended off the back foot.
Length ball outside off and Sharjeel swings for it but the slant of the delivery beats him.
In the channel outside off, some gentle swing, Sharjeel shoulders arms.
Short and wide outside off, cut to the man at point.
DAVID WILLEY bowls from the other end.
Length ball on middle and off, blocked off the back foot to the leg side.
Good length outside off, Azhar goes for the cut but gets a bottom edge to the off side.
Length ball on off, worked towards short mid-wicket.
Short and wide outside off, Khan flashes at it and gets a thick edge down to third man for a single.
Good length outside off, no shot offered to that one.
Good length on middle and leg, Azhar works it away on the leg side. Won't make the fence but they'll get three.
Welcome back to the run chase. The players are back in the middle. Sharjeel Khan and Azhar Ali to open the batting. It shall be Chris Woakes to begin the bowling proceedings.
